In Foundation/Sobolev/TestFunction.lean, or JSpace.lean if the imports allow:

def CKN.WeakTestFunction.reflect (κ : Vec3 → ℝ) (hκ : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) κ) (hκc : HasCompactSupport κ) (x : Vec3) : CKN.WeakTestFunction (Set.univ : Set Vec3) :=
  ⟨fun y => κ (x - y), hκ.comp (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id), hκc.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.subLeft x), Set.subset_univ _⟩

theorem CKN.WeakTestFunction.reflect_partialDeriv (κ hκ hκc x) (i : Fin 3) (y : Vec3) :
    (CKN.WeakTestFunction.reflect κ hκ hκc x).partialDeriv i y = -(fderiv ℝ κ (x - y)) (CKN.basisVec i)

Proof sketch: the proof is the existing block with κ in place of η. Show `HasFDerivAt (fun z => x - z) (-id) y` and `HasFDerivAt κ (fderiv ℝ κ (x - y)) (x - y)`. Compose them, take `.fderiv`, and evaluate at `basisVec i`. The proof of the second statement is exactly the current lines 46–55 of the target.

claims.reason: The block at lines 102–111 is composition of existing API, not repeated mathematical reasoning. `ψ.partialDeriv i` is by definition `fderiv ℝ ψ.toFun · (basisVec i)`, so it is `spatialDeriv ψ i`. Continuity, smoothness and compact support are already supplied by `CKN.contDiff_spatialDeriv_smooth` and `CKN.hasCompactSupport_spatialDeriv`, which have a public version in Pressure/SpatialDerivSupport.lean. Other copies (JSpaceMollify.lean 215–224, RegularisedInitialData.lean 472–481) already use `contDiff_spatialDeriv_smooth`. The L² step is `Continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport`, a single Mathlib call. Each repetition is three one-line API applications: `continuous_fderiv … clm_apply`, `fderiv_apply`, `memLp_of_hasCompactSupport`. That is routine regularity boilerplate, and a `WeakTestFunction.memLp_partialDeriv` lemma would be a thin wrapper around existing API. This is at most a small cleanup under some other rubric. The pairing in the other proofs (for example LocalSolutionDivFreePairing) also uses different integrability hypotheses, so the copies are not one uniform argument.
